title: Einsum Trees: An Abstraction for Optimizing the Execution of Tensor Expressions
problem: Optimizing the execution of multi-operand einsum tensor expressions requires co-optimizing both the contraction path (order of binary contractions) and the data layout of intermediate tensors, but these two problems have been studied in isolation, leading to suboptimal global execution performance.
motivation: Tensor contraction workloads in ML and scientific computing are highly sensitive to memory layout and contraction ordering; separate optimization of each leaves significant performance on the table.
method: Einsum Tree IR represents a sequence of tensor contractions (step-by-step combinations of multi-dimensional arrays) as a tree structure, then chooses how to arrange the data for all contractions together, rather than deciding separately for each one. This global approach reduces how much data needs to move between the CPU's main memory and its fast cache. The optimized contraction sequences execute on standard CPUs (Arm and x86) using existing high-performance tensor libraries.
key_novelty: Einsum Tree IR optimizes how tensor data is arranged across an entire sequence of contractions at once to minimize data movement, rather than optimizing each contraction's data arrangement separately.
contributions: Einsum Tree IR: an intermediate representation for globally optimizing data layout for a given contraction path
Global data-layout optimization algorithm operating on the full contraction tree
Evaluation on Arm and x86 server and desktop processors demonstrating improved execution time over local optimization

metrics.other: improved overall einsum execution times vs. locally optimized contraction paths on Arm and x86

limitations: Evaluation targets CPU only; GPU/accelerator backends are not evaluated.
primary_theme: global tensor data-layout optimization via Einsum Tree IR
